_ THE POLITICS OF REVOLUTIONARY
ANTI              TIPERIALISM




 ns                               BOLIVIGAL STATEMENT

 7                     eo         WEATHER
                                   | URESRGROUND

         PRINTED UNBDERGROUN.
         IN THE U.S.
     | FOR THE PEOPLE
     Fa kaeaeTE   ES        ANN    a   ae

                                                        “1
. Sisters and brothers,


            Here is PRAIRIE FIRE, our political ideology —a strategy for
  anti-imperialism and revolution inside the imperial US, It comes out of our
  own practice of the last five years and reflects a diversity of experiences.
  This paper is not the product of one or two people, nor even a small handful
  of us, Rather PRAIRIE FIRE represents thé polities and collective efforts of
  an organization, It has been the focus of our study groups and our political
  education. It has been chewed on and shaped in Gountless conversations,
  struggles and written pages. It has travelled around the country, growing,
  developing thru the attempt to understand the shape of world forces and the      ee
                                                                                   fr"
                                                                                     a

  revolutionary possibilities before us. ‘The paper was rewritten four times and
  collectively adopted as the political statement.ofthe Weather Underground.
  The twelve-month process of writing PRAIRIE FIRE, squeezed between
  on-going work and practice and action, has now. reached a kind of end-point, .
  A cycle is done.                             -             mo


            We undertook this analysis to explain the changes in US and world
  ‘conditions since the Vietnam ceasefire and to evaluate the consequences of
  the Vietnamese victory, We have come some distance in evaluating the
  political situation, the priorities for revolutionary work since we began this
  writing. Now many more revolutionaries will need to shape and change the
  paper. The politics cannot be realized unless and until the content of the
   program is activated in thousands of situations, among thousands of people    “
  in the coming period. PRAIRIE FIRE will be       a growing thing.           ae



           We hope the paper opens a dialectic among those in the mass and         os
  clandestine movements; we      hope people       will take PRAIRIE   FIRE as
  seriously as we do, study the content and write and publish their views of
  the paper as well as their analysis of their own practice. We will respond as
  best we can,       .                         :



       7 Our movement urgently needs a conerete analysis of the particular :
  conditions of our time and place. We need strategy. We necd to battle fora
  correct ideology and'win people over. In this way we create the conditions                                                 i
  for the development of a successful revolutionary movement and party. We:                 *                                !
  need a revolutionary communist party in order to lead the struggle, give                      .                            !
 .coherence and dircetion to the fight, seize power and build the new society.
     Getting from here to there is a process of coming together in a disciplined                        .                 {
     way. around ideology and strategy, developing an analysis of our real                      .                        a
     conditions, mobilizing a base among the US people, building principled                                               i
     relationships to Third World struggle, and accumulating practice in struggle                                         '
     against US imperialism.                                 .                 :                                oa


           .   PRAIRIE      FIRE     is written     to   communist-mindéd         people,
     independent ofganizers and anti-imperialists; those who carry the traditions
     and lessons of the struggles of the last decade, those who. join in the struggles
     of today. PRAIRIE FIRE is written to all sisters and brothers who are                                                   :
     engaged in armed struggle against the enemy. It is written to prisoners,                                        -
     women’s groups, collectives, study groups, workers’ erganizing committees,                                          ,
     communes, GI organizers, consciousness-raising groups, veterans, community
     groups and revolutionaries of all- kinds; to all who will read, criticize and                          r                    :
     bring its content to life in practice. {tiiswritten asan argument against those            .
     whooppose action and hold back the struggle.

       ,             FIRE is based on a helief that the duty of a revolutionary
     is to make the revolution. This is not an abstraction, Jt means that
- revolutionaries must make a profound commitment to the future of
   humanity, apply our limited knowledge and, experience to understand an -
   ever-changing situation, organize the masses of people and build the fight. It
   means that struggle and risk and hard work and adversity will become a way of                                                 ;
 . Hfe, that the “only certainty will be constant ehange, that the only                                                          i
   possibilities are victory or death.    0                     -                 _                                              |

                                                                                                                                 |
                                                                                                                                 |
 .              We have only begun. At this time, the unity and consolidation of                                                 ’
      anti-imperialist forces around a revolutionary program is an urgent and
      pressing strategic necessity, PRAIRIE FIRE is offered ds a contribution to
     ¢his unity of action and Purpose. Now it is in your hands.

                            TIMOTHY        FRANCIS          LEARY,          JR.     was        interviewed             at the
           office of the California Department of Corrections, 3415
           Fletcher Avenue, Suite 201,  Also present at the beginning
           of the interview was               a Special Agent of the                                                                        b6
           California Department of Corrections.                                                                                            b7C

                          The       interview commenced at 10:16 a.m. at which                                                time
           Special      Agent       R. J. IA JEUNZSSE, JR. presented Mr. LEARY                                                a
           form    entitled,           “Interrogation;                  Advice        of Rights".              After          reading
           the    form LEARY signed the Waiver                              of Rights               section     of      the    form
           and    the interview commenced.                                                                        z

                      Interviewing Agent personnel had in their possession
           considerable papers, documents, correspondence and other
           memorabilia beldénging to LEARY which had been obtained on
           July 16, LO74, from personnel of the Drug Enforcement
           Administration              (DEA),      Los Angeles,                 California.

           was    a letter on blue                stationery directed                          to PTMOTHY             LEARY,
           Le Dauphin Number One, Villers SVR - Orion, Switzerland.”

           London W. 9, Englend."   Upon gxamining this letter LEARY
           identified it as one sent to him in November 1971, from
           ELEANOR and MICHAEL KENNEDY,   The contents of the letter                                                          are:

              With    respect   to the     above     described           letter     LEARY
explained it was directed           to him        while he was Living in
Switzerland folhowing his           escape        in the California Prison
System in 1970.

          As best he can now recall the letter followed a
personal visit to him madé by the KENNEDYs when LEARY was
living in Villars, V.D., Switzerland, probably in late
September or early October 1971.

            LEARY was questioned concerning his marriage to
the former ROSEMARY WOODRUFF,     He explained they were
married December 12, 1968, at the estate of BILLY HITCHCOCK
in Millbrook, Dutchess County, New York.      Present as a legal
witness to the marriage was HITCHCOCK's sister, MARGARET
MELLON HITCHCOCK,     Also present at the wedding were numerous
other   people   LEARY stated the marriage was performed by
                    and ordain      minister      of    "some Hindusect"        which
he recalis was named           ‘Tid
           LEARY considers the marriage to have been a legal
one and that it should have been recorded in Albany, New York,
He stated he recalls getting the license for the marriage
in the town hall in Milibrook, New York,   The former MARY
MELLON HITCHCOCK is now married to WALTER BOWARD and they are
living in Tucson, Arizona.

          LEARY explained that he and                   ROSEMARY WOODRUFF
was subsequently remarried on several                   other occasions in
different marital rites none of which                   was legally recorded.

                    aided him in his escape from the San Luis Obigps, California,

              fhe Weatherman erovm, now commonly                           .

              as a faction of the Students for a
              Democratic Society (SDS).   A Weather~
              man ideological paper entitled “You
              Don't Need a Weatherman to Know Which
              Way the Wind Blows", prepared in June,
              1969,    stated     the    basis    philosophy        of
              this    group   is Marxist-Leninist             in
              content    but with        strong    advocacy        that
              action, not theory, would bring about
             -xevolution in the United States,   In
              Mid-February, 1970, members of the
              Weatherman entered an underground
              status with an intended program of
              "strategic sabotage” with police and
              military     installations          as primary
              targets.

              Current Federal warrants are outstanding
              for a number of Weatherman wanted for vio-
              lations of Federal statutes and local
              criminal violations.    Since 1970, the
              Weather, Underground has claimed responsi-
              bility for a number of bombings, including
              the United States Capitol Buidding in
              March, 1971; the Pentagon Building in May,
              1972; the ITT Building in NYC in September,
              1973; the Office of the California State
              Attorney General, Los Angeles, in May,
              1974; and the Gulf Oil Corporation Building,
              Pittsburgh, in dune, 1974,    In October, 1973,
              @ Weatherman fugitive, in a letter to the
              press, encouraged other revolutionaries    to
              assumean underground status, noting that the
              underground provides a revolutionary haven for
              operations looking toward the violent over-

            Co]                  Me All's            Information         Services
Company,     1419   West   Fifth   St.,         on        5/28/74,     advised    that
postal meter number 610394 is one of six meter numbers
assigned to Mc All's Information Services Company (MISCO).
This number corresponds to a postal meter which is used in
processing direct mailing of more than 200 pieces of business
mail.   How it should happen that this meter number would appear                                  b7¢c
upon an envelope bearing a private individuals's name
and return address is unknown to him.             stated
that it is possible that an employée could run any number
of blank envelopes through the postal meter he was operating
and thereafter use those envelopes on a personal basis.
However, it is unlikely that an employee would run blank
envelopes through a machine being operated by him, as
mailings are controlled by job orders which specify the
precise number of pieces being mailed, and that number must
correspond with the count of items passed through the meter.
Another possibility is that return envelopes mailed as enclosures
to a direct mailing had been removed from the direct mailing
literature at the point of delivery and, after the return
address had been ae              ee by the recipient as a
personal envelope.            noted that approximately 60
employees had been utilized on the direct mail postal meters
since 1/1/74, but that it would be possible to compile a list
of operators of the postal meter bearing number Cie         that
should be necessary.    [7 _]checked the current and past
employee rosters for MISCO and advised that he could locate
no current or   past employee identifiable with JOSEPH L. RAUH

Result       of    examination:

                   Specimens       ¢¢16 through            Q63    were    examined          to determine
if they contain coded or encrypted material.    Most of these
specimens consist of transcripts of textual material
typical of "free association" writing.    This type of writing,
presumably meant to represent the thought process,   does not
always produce logical, complete sentences, and lends itself
particularly well to codes of the "veiled" or “double
meaning" variety.   In this type of code, certain segments of
seemingly innocuous statements hold special meanings obvious
only to the communicators.   These “veiled" meanings may have
been    derived          from    particular          significant          events       in the
experience of the correspondents or may have been previously
determined and set forth as an arbitrarily selected group
ef equivalents.

           Without benefit of Timothy Leary’s explanation of
the meanings of the coded terms related to his escape and the
participants therein, it is possible to state that the texts


Page     5
CR-14253          PL
                                                           37
ef specimens Q34, 35, 37, 39, 40, 41, 42, 44, 45, 46, 52
and Qc50 and 51 are consistent with the type of text
normally employed to transmit messages having "veiled"
Meanings.   The Qc50 and 51 photocopies of letters from
Timothy to Rosemary Leary, when viewed independent of
Timothy Leary's explanation of coded terms, but in light
of subsequent events, i.e., the escape, can be said to
refer, generally,   to the escape of Leary from prison.
Especially significant in this conclusion are the
following       statements    in specimens          Qc50   and   51 respectively:

            “The Beckett manuscript  (referring to the escape
plian)...should leave here Thursday or Friday.     When you get
it read it carefully beloved.     It is a very important story...
Listen to thé words carefully and you will see that it carries
the solution to ail our problems.     This man-uscript will
bring everyone together and end paranoia, distrust and
separation.”

                "Beloved...please contact MK and communicate                      to
him    the    underlying message of my last two letters..."

           Explanations of Timothy Leary as to the meanings
of symbols and statements contained in submitted specimens
are plausible and consistent with subsequent events.
No discrepancies in his interpretation of the true meaning
of the specimens were noted.

                 Specimens   Qcl6   through        Q63   are   being   retained    in
Bureau       file.

“             ry      Mrs. VERL WOODRUFF, “¥o6s9 Lower Azusa Road,
            (telephone 444-8876) was contacted at her residence.
           Mrs. WOODRUFF              's the mother            of ROSMARTE            LEARY,       nee
           Woodruff.

                      Mrs. WOODRUFF was advised that the purpose of
           the interview was designed to furnish information to her
           so -that she might subsequently forward it on to her daughter
           for proper evaluation.   Mrs. WOODRUFF was told that various
           law enforcement agencies, including the FBI, were attempting
           to locate ROSMARIES LEARY to interview her regarding any knowledge
           she might have of the events leading up to the escape of TIMOTHY
           LEARY from the California Prison System ‘n September 1970.

                       Mrs. WOODRUFF was further advised that in all
            probability ROSMARIE LEARY would be taken into custody by
            Orange County, California, authorities in the event she
            decided to make herself available for interview inasmuch
            as she is in violation of her probationary status with that
            agency.              7

                            Mrs, WOODRUFF professed not to know of                                       the whereabouts
            of her       daughter nor is she able to contact her.

                       She explainedthat the last time she and her husband
           .saw their daughter was when ROSMARIE appeared “at the WOODRUFF
            residence shortly before she left the country.   They next heard
            from her when she and TIMOTHY LEARY telephonically contacted then
            from Algiers.   On the occasion that ROSMARIE visited ner parents
           ‘prior to contacting them from Algiers TIMOTHY LEARY was still
            incarcerated in the California Prison Systen.

                       Mrs. WOODRUFF was advised that in the event she is
            able to contact her daughter that her daugher be advised of _
            the United States Government's interest in talking with her
            for the purpose of obtaining information which might tend to
            corroborate information furnished ty TIMOTHY LEARY regarding
            his escape.

             During      this meeting,    the LEARY    archives   were

their own purposes.           ,
